# IOStreams

> IOStreams is a Ruby gem for streaming I/O that makes file formats, compression, encryption,
> and storage mechanisms (local file, S3, Google Cloud Storage, SFTP, HTTP) transparent to the application. Files of
> any size are processed one block at a time without loading them into memory.

The public entry points are `IOStreams.path(...)`, `IOStreams.join(...)` and `IOStreams.stream(io)`,
which return a path or stream. Its settings describe the file: `#stream`/`#option` for compression and
encryption, `#encoding` for its text, `#format` and `#schema` for its rows and records, `#as` for the contract that a program reads them through, and `#raw` to
read and write it as stored. It is read and written with `#each`, `#reader`, `#writer`, `#read`,
`#write`, `#copy_from`, `#copy_to` and `#move_to`, in the `:stream`, `:line`, `:array`, `:hash`, `:record` or `:slice`
mode.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/): what IOStreams is, why it exists, a quick tour, how it works, common tasks with a line of code each, what it supports, and the optional gems to install for each feature.
- [Tutorial](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/tutorial): step-by-step introduction to writing and reading files, lines, rows and records, typed records with a contract, drafting a contract from a file, the same records from CSV, JSON and Excel, storage, encodings, errors and copies.
- [Reading and Writing](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/streams): the `:stream`, `:line`, `:array`, `:hash`, `:record` and `:slice` modes, values that are not valid and `on_invalid:`, what a failed write keeps, lines, text encodings with `#encoding`, `#raw`, and the streams that a file name implies.
- [Paths](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/path): where a file is stored (local disk, S3, Google Cloud Storage with `gs://`, which is experimental, SFTP, HTTP), the options of each store, and the operations on a path, such as listing, joining and deleting.
- [File Formats](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/formats): CSV, PSV, JSON Lines, fixed width, Excel and Parquet files, plain text, how the format is chosen, and what each format needs of a schema.
- [Contracts](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/contracts): reading the same records from any source with a contract, the fields that a program needs and their types, set with `#as`: `IOStreams::Contract`, declared as a class with `field`, or built from a Hash, records of a contract with `each(:record)`, checking a source with `#validate_contract!`, reporting invalid rows with `on_invalid:`, drafting a contract with `#infer_schema(sample:)` and `#to_dsl`, every field in its order, missing columns raising before the first row, writing through a contract, and a file with a schema of its own, such as fixed width.
- [Schemas](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/schemas): describing the columns of a file with a schema, a Frictionless Table Schema set with `#schema`, as a Hash or a JSON file: `#infer_schema` and the schema that a source declares, the types of fields (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `time`, `duration`, `object`, `array`, `any`), matching columns to fields with aliases, `keyType`, `fieldsMatch`, `extraColumns`, required fields and `allowBlank`, and every schema and field property, which contracts share.
- [Compression and Encryption](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/extensions): the gzip, bzip2, zip, Zstandard, PGP and Symmetric Encryption streams and their options.
- [Copying and Moving](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/copy_files): `#copy_from`, `#copy_to` and `#move_to`, converting compression, encryption and format on the way, the contract or types that a copy hands to its target, and what a failed copy leaves.
- [Exporting Queries](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/queries): exporting the rows of an Active Record query to any format and store with `copy_from(relation, mode: :hash)`, reading them with `IOStreams.stream(relation)`, one query or `in_batches`, the schema of the types of its columns and the columns that need a type, such as JSON for Parquet, the connection of its own that a query is read on, how PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite stream a query, and its failures.
- [Background Jobs](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/background_jobs): processing large files and queries in background jobs with Active Job, Sidekiq or any job queue: one job per slice of rows (`each(:slice)`, a store of slices with `IOStreams::Slice::Target`, `slice.to_h` and `IOStreams.slice`, `IOStreams.stream(slice)`), where to keep the slices, batches, a job that resumes at its cursor with `resume_at:` (Active Job continuations, Sidekiq iterable jobs, job-iteration), files of lines, failures and retries, and writing the results to one file with `writer(:slice)`.
- [Errors](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/errors): rescuing a missing file, a file that cannot be accessed, or a server that cannot be reached, the same way wherever the file is stored, with `IOStreams::Errors::NotFound`, `PermissionDenied` and `Unavailable`, and the other exceptions that IOStreams raises.
- [PGP Encryption](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/pgp): reading, writing, signing and verifying PGP files with GnuPG, and managing keys.
- [Configuration](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/config): keeping paths in configuration, named roots with `IOStreams.add_root`, the temp directory and when temp files are used, the logger, and every process-wide setting.
- [Security](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/security): allowed paths, untrusted names and urls, keeping credentials out of logs, uploaded files, and processing PGP files safely.
- [Extending IOStreams](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/extending): registering a format for a file name extension, and a path class for a url scheme.
- [Upgrading IOStreams](https://iostreams.reidmorrison.com/upgrading): changes that may need updates to your application when upgrading to v3.0, v2.1 or v2.0.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/reidmorrison/iostreams): source code, issue tracker, and CONTRIBUTING.md for the design philosophy and architecture behind the reader/writer pipeline.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/reidmorrison/iostreams/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): release history.
